areas.why: the skill names the checks it runs (claude_deny.py --check and --merge, apply --overlay, the verdict line) and each reads as written on 2026-11-23; a rule added to the deny list does not change it
the rule says deny and hookify rules block one-way doors, not which entries the list holds; a rule added to it does not change what the doc says

the rule routes work and money by the account's facts, which account.example.json holds; ci-standard.yml's own checks are in rules/compute-detail.md, which keeps that area

the doc says voice_lint.py lists the banned patterns, so a pattern added there is read from the tool, not restated here
the page routes a need to a file; broken_links catches a moved target, and a reworded SECURITY.md or CONTRIBUTING.md leaves it true
the on-demand half of rules/keys.md, so it follows that rule and the account's keys fields, not every sibling rule

params.areas_readme: First match wins. Each doc maps to the files it describes: a change there can make the doc wrong, a change to a sibling doc cannot. THREAT-MODEL.md and tools/THREAT-MODEL.md each take the code their rows describe, from the paths of security.threat_model_current, the guard rules and the Comfy guard. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md adopts an outside standard, so it is a record. The wiki pages take what they link to and the workflow that publishes them. Any other doc covers its own folder.

goal_source: Git Crafter goal, 2026-11-10: every reader doc here holds a diagram, a chart or a drill-down, since the owner asks for visual and interactive docs first (rules/writing-and-gates.md); the template goal is 80. Sources: GitHub Docs: Creating diagrams; GitHub Docs: Organizing information with collapsed sections

Git Crafter goal, 2026-11-10: no doc under 50% visual lines, since the owner asks for every doc to be as visual as possible, with as little text as possible (rules/writing-and-gates.md, Visual first); the template goal is 20%. Source: Microsoft Style Guide: Scannable content (dense text set out as lists and tables)
